Scope: /api/meta must report a build identity that tracks redeploys, plus a human-authorised second item (upgrade trigger on the boilerplate.py ponytail marker, and a false ponytail-marker count in a TODO debt row). The row was blocked as (dashboard) on a false premise: the 2026-08-17 console check found no sha to borrow because ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA is BUILD-phase only. So it became a repo change (zbpack build_command writes BUILD_SHA, gitignored; a fastapi-free build_id.py resolves it) and needed no dashboard access. S2 s own validation gate is UNRUN and unrunnable from here - no agent can run a Zeabur build - and clears by curling the live instance across TWO redeploys, since the sha must MOVE, not merely exist. Round 1 (1H/4M/4L): the HIGH was an unvalidated GIT_SHA branch rendering latest/main/an unexpanded $ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA as build labels while the ADR claimed validation at every step; three MEDIUM were documents of record contradicting the tree (a GIT_DIR leak claimed closed but open on the production path, 16-vs-18 failures against the artifact cited as its own evidence, a precedence table published as enforced while a git-first resolver stayed green at 0 failures). Round 2 (0H/3M/3L): 8 of 9 closed, R4 RELOCATED - the new _temp_repo precedence assertions went silently vacuous under an absolute GIT_INDEX_FILE, i.e. exactly the linked-worktree condition this PR was authored in, so the falsifier was dead where the gate runs; and R10 was a false RED the round-1 repair introduced. Round 3: APPROVED, both falsifiers measured live again (M6=2 under GIT_INDEX_FILE, M11=1) and M8 STRENGTHENED to 3 under an ambient GIT_DIR rather than weakened. All 14 mutation counts independently reproduced. The implementer also retracted its own round-1 anomaly explanation: a byte-identical reordering mutation rewritten inside one mtime second makes Python serve a stale .pyc, invalidate_caches insufficient - reproduced and confirmed by the reviewer. Orchestrator ran the gate independently at every transition and merged origin/main TWICE mid-loop (PR #30/T3, then PR #32/T5); the second collided on ADR number 027 and on prompts/013, so this branch renumbered to ADR-028 / prompts-014 - that merge was orchestrator work and was put into round 3 scope as unreviewed rather than taken on trust. Ledger-only: take verified-closed rows out of the debt working set. The human ruled the destination (delete outright, no archive, no ADR-022 amendment) and earlier ruled the audit scope. THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE ORCHESTRATOR'S AUDIT WAS WRONG ON 2 OF THE 5 ROWS IT PROPOSED: it classified by asking whether a row said CLOSED, which is the naive check the audit existed to beat. The implementer refused both and verified against the artifacts instead -- in each, the CLOSED marker covered sub-parts while the row TITLE named the part still open (PR #11 R22 / axp-2008, part 3 open, case has no text_contains; bench._demo / DOC_ALLOW, no assertion at :879+). Round 1 confirmed all five row calls correct and found both findings in the NEW rows' prose: one mis-read ADR-021 (which already publishes 26 in the same sentence, reconciling twice over), the other cited a tasks/reviews/ artifact that did not exist. Round 2: R1/R2 closed; the committed audit artifact then contradicted ITSELF on the debt-row count (88 vs 87, same commit) and every count in both artifacts was off by one -- including a post_merge_note added that same round specifically to fix a stale integer. Round 3: APPROVED, and the root cause was independently reproduced rather than accepted: the derivation subtracted header AND separator, but the grep pattern for a data row never matches the dashed separator line, so every figure was uniformly one low -- which is why 're-derive it' alone failed four times. The implementer chose to DROP every count nothing consumes rather than correct them, on this PR's own thesis that an unguarded integer with no consumer rots. It also declined to overclaim: whether a struck-through title is safer than an inline CLOSED marker is named as the open question, since both refusals were inline markers. Two mid-loop merges (PR #41 / D3 struck a 23rd row and falsified our own count; the orchestrator resolved the conflict and relayed the correction). Fourth branch/id collision of the session -- task/D2 was PR #39's and task/D3 was held by a live session, so the branch was renamed descriptively. Human interventions: 2 (destination ruling; earlier audit-scope ruling).

TWO ADJUDICATIONS WENT AGAINST THE REVIEWER AND BOTH WERE CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ARGUMENT. Probing a live DOM: under visibility:hidden offsetParent!==null is TRUE and the box is 349x636, so the finding as written would have passed the finding own mutation. Verified independently by the orchestrator and again by the round-2 reviewer. (2) R6 was split rather than routed whole - the instrument gap (checkVisibility answers RENDERED, not ON SCREEN; #source at left:-9999px passes at exit 0) went to debt because the shipped layout is correct at every measured width, while the one element meeting the dishonest-claim bar, prompts/019 calling it the native API for the question actually being asked, was corrected in place. No round-3 review was opened for the final text-only repair; the orchestrator proved it text-only by stripping every HTML comment from index.html at both commits and comparing (IDENTICAL), and that call is recorded in pr46-r2.json.
